answer: To resist Sybils an agent economy can force every new identity to compute a sequential verifiable delay function whose length grows with the size of its funding cluster. An honest agent on a single island pays a fixed short delay; a gale of clones sharing one wallet faces quadratic growth in the required chain of sequential steps. The reef of honest validators only accepts the proof, so the attacker must burn real wall-clock compute proportional to N squared before any of the N identities can earn, rendering large farms unprofitable.
